title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Improve continuous-batcher scheduling: better fairness, starvation prevention, adaptive timeouts and observability. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: The continuous-batcher scheduler occasionally showed starvation of low-priority request classes under peak load and had brittle static timeouts that either hurt tail latency or reduced throughput. This change introduces a set of scheduler and policy improvements aimed at reducing starvation, improving fairness across priority classes, and making per-batch timeouts adaptive to observed latency distributions. Summary of changes: 1) Multi-level per-priority queues with aging-based promotion: requests live in priority buckets and are promoted after a configurable age threshold to prevent starvation of low-priority classes. 2) Adaptive timeouts: batcher timeouts are computed per-queue from recent latency percentiles (sliding window p50/p95), with configurable caps and floor values to avoid pathological values. 3) Queue-level backpressure and admission controls: when queues exceed configured high-water marks we apply tail-drop and signal backpressure to upstream request routers. 4) Sharded, lock-free counters and per-shard metrics to reduce contention under high concurrency. 5) New metrics and traces to observe wait-time distributions, promotions, and timeout adjustments. 6) CI/unit/perf tests and a benchmark harness update that measures P50/P95/P99 behavior under mixed-priority workloads. The description below lists commits, changed files, test/benchmark summaries, and review discussion. No user-visible API changes; all knobs are configuration flags under batcher.schedule.* and default to safe values.

review_comments: Elena Rodriguez (2026-01-14): This is a strong direction. Two concerns: 1) how are we ensuring the promotion path doesn't cause convoys? 2) locking on metrics in queue hot-path could be costly. Can you add contention benchmarks and consider per-shard counters?

Samir Patel (2026-01-15): Addressed both. Scheduler now promotes using an atomic compare-and-swap on queue headers and promotions are staggered by a jitter factor to avoid convoying. Metrics are per-shard and aggregated by the exporter - added a microbenchmark showing ~2% reduced throughput vs baseline but large reduction in contention spikes.

Noah Kim (2026-01-16): The adaptive timeout algorithm looks good but we should cap growth to avoid cascading large timeouts on transient spikes. Also add a debug metric showing the computed timeout per-queue for at least p50/p95 samples.
Samir Patel (2026-01-16): Added configurable cap (batcher.schedule.timeout_cap_ms) and a computed_timeout gauge (batcher_queue_computed_timeout_ms) emitted every evaluation window.
